hypotheses.binder: (hupper : ∀ n x, x ∈ s.domain → ‖N n x‖ ≤ M)
hypotheses.justification: A uniform upper bound on N is not needed for the conclusion. The lower bound and hb give ‖N n x‖ ≥ b > 0, so the inverse-square factor is smooth on the domain. Its derivatives are finite sums of products of derivatives of N divided by powers of ‖N‖²; the lower bound controls those denominators, while hN supplies polynomial-growth bounds for the numerator factors. Thus the inverse-square factor, and hence the pressure coefficient and final band-scaled expression, retain the required class bounds without hupper. This also covers the zero case: the lower bound excludes N = 0 wherever the domain is nonempty, and an empty domain makes the pointwise bounds vacuous.
